A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP/OpenCLIP bias audit despite the changed title. All 11 pages of v3 and 20 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable. Original tables, figures and prompt lists can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original FairFace and PATA evaluations, including demographic bias scores and harmful-label frequencies across model sizes and pretraining corpora.

after.justification: v5 retains those evaluations and adds original debiasing comparisons, synthetic-image controls, calibration results and prompt-sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The controlled audit, CLIP/OpenCLIP architectures, contrastive objective and original probing tasks are retained. v5 evaluates three existing debiasing methods but introduces no new author-proposed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: FairFace, PATA and the original demographic and trait tasks remain. v5 adds 19 generated portraits intended to be feature-neutral as a distinct control scenario, and COCO2017 for SANER training. The expanded description of PATA's scene context does not establish a newly added benchmark.

E2.justification: v3 compares untreated CLIP/OpenCLIP checkpoints. v5 adds Bias Prompts comparisons for both families and Prompt Array and SANER comparisons for OpenCLIP, with results in Table 3 and Figures 5–8.

E3.justification: v5 introduces mitigation-training protocols, including three-epoch Prompt Array training and five-epoch SANER training. New appendix protocols evaluate 19 control portraits, calibrate directional bias using seven bins, and test three prompt templates on 3,948 PATA images. These are added experimental designs; the original checkpoint grid and inference settings remain.

E4.justification: New Appendices A–C test whether bias persists on intended-neutral images, how directional-bias magnitude relates to harmful predictions, and sensitivity to prompt wording. These introduce substantive control, calibration and robustness analyses beyond v3's retained size/source comparisons.

E5.justification: Table 5 newly reports descriptive dispersion through the mean and standard deviation of pairwise cosine similarities among control portraits. Existing 95% bootstrap-confidence-interval reporting is retained. No increased seed or repeated-run count is reported; Appendix C mentions standard deviations, but Table 7 displays means and template differences instead.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and delta-table values are unchanged, including v3 Table 3 becoming v5 Table 4. v5 adds extensive mitigation and appendix results. For example, its new FairFace CLIP-B/32 Bias Prompts row reports gender–crime bias of 0.11 versus 1.19 untreated, while crime-label frequency is 28.18% versus 8%, demonstrating a new intervention trade-off.

T1.justification: The contrastive loss and pairwise MaxSkew formula remain. Appendices A–B introduce directional-bias and conditional-harm calibration definitions, including an elbow threshold. v3's assertion that the pairwise mean upper-bounds multiclass inequality disappears. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Beyond retained claims that scaling can worsen bias, v5 makes comparative debiasing and source/size-dependent mitigation efficacy central contributions. Its introduction also changes from describing OpenCLIP as more gender-biased to saying LAION improves gender fairness, although Section 4.4 retains the former statement.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations involving mitigation over-correction, lexical coverage, neutral contexts and embedding geometry, together with recommendations against transferring harm between demographic axes. It also adds interpretations of the appendix controls and calibration. Expanded limitations acknowledge untested sizes/scales and the inability to inspect proprietary data or disentangle scale from curation policies.

D1.justification: Section 3.6 adds mitigation implementation information: released projection matrices, Prompt Array training on 90k FairFace plus 90k LAION images with a 0.05 contrastive-loss weight, and SANER training on COCO2017. Appendix A supplies generators and an example control-image prompt. Original resolution, hardware and runtime disclosures remain; no usable code URL is added.

R1.justification: v5 adds Chuang et al. (2023) and Hirota et al. (2025), and expands discussion connecting Bias Prompts, Prompt Array and SANER to the audit. The broader dataset-bias and scaling literature remains substantially intact; bibliographic corrections do not themselves constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from Size ≠ Fairness to Data Matters Most, and composition/decomposition terminology becomes source. Selected abstract, contribution, metric-explanation and conclusion passages are rewritten. The main section sequence and much original prose remain; the original prompt appendix moves from A to D.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting, substantially resizing and relocating displays. v5 adds four tables and six figures, including mitigation panels, the portrait montage and calibration plot. Original Figures 1–3 are reused, Figure 4 is cropped, and the original race-delta table is renumbered.

improvement.justification: v5 adds broader mitigation evidence, clearer metric explanations, robustness checks and more explicit limitations. However, important new conclusions conflict with their support: SANER's claimed consistent race–agency reduction contradicts its 0.11 versus untreated 0.05 score for FairFace OpenCLIP-B/32@2B, and Figure 10 shows only one low-bias bin despite describing an elbow and saturation. These inconsistencies undermine the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
